summary: Returns the value after checking that it is not an object.
description: The test is `typeof value === "object"` with `null` excluded, so arrays, dates and class instances all count, while a function does not. `isObjectLike` is the one that also accepts functions.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, with an object excluded from its type.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireNonObject(null); // => null
requireNonObject("abc"); // => "abc"
requireNonObject({}); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonObject([]); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
